title: A saved colour dropped on a layer row paints the part it names
goal: A saved text style can now be let go on a row in the layers list. A saved colour still cannot: aiming a colour tile at a row does nothing and says nothing. The open question is what a colour on a row should paint, because a row is not a colour well: a shape has a fill and an outline, text has its own colour, and a screenshot has neither.
notes:
Split out of a-saved-style-can-be-dropped-on-a-row-in-the-lay, which shipped the TEXT STYLE half on 2026-09-09. The two do not share a target resolution and the task file said to split them if they did not.

What is already there to build on. The layers row is now a drop target for the app own pasteboard types: Sources/Photonz/LayersPanel.swift, LayerRowDropDelegate, which reads TextStyleDrag.payloadInFlight() first and falls through to the row and file paths. ColorDrag.payloadInFlight() is the colour twin and already exists. The row mark and the one line under the list are StyleRowDrop / StyleRowMarking (Sources/PhotonzCore/StyleRowMarking.swift) plus StyleRowDropNote in LayersPanel.swift, and both are written around TextStyleDrop.Answer, so a colour answer either needs the same shape or the mark needs to carry either kind.

The hard part is not the plumbing, it is WHICH part a colour lands on. ColorDrop.Target is built around a named part (Fill, Outline, Shadow) that a swatch row supplies; a layer row supplies none. Candidate rule: the first colour row the inspector would show for that layer, which is Text for text and Fill for a shape. That is a product judgment about a silent choice among several parts, so open a decision on it before building rather than guessing, and write the options in terms of what the line under the list would say.
acceptance: Letting go of a saved colour on a layer row paints one named part of that layer, and the line the list says names the part before you let go
A row with no part a colour could land on says so in the same voice the text style refusal uses
The drop is one undo step, and undo puts the row back exactly as it was
A row that is locked refuses, the way it refuses a text style
A walk drives it end to end (Scripts/playtest/, dragTile with onto)

log.note: Adversarial review before building. (1) A colour well says what it paints by its own name; a layer ROW says only the layer name, so the whole feature rests on the line under the list naming the part before the drop. That line already exists and the text style half proved it. (2) The choice is narrower than the task feared: a box has Fill and nothing else, words have Text and nothing else, an arrow has its Line plus a Head only when it ends in one. Several parts to choose from is really just an arrow with a head or a caption, and a measurement with its chip, and in every one of those the first part is the thing the layer IS. (3) What it buys over today: recolouring a row you are NOT editing without losing your selection. Real but modest, so the shortest version wins and a hover-to-unfold parts menu is overbuilt. (4) No gesture collision: colour is already a DragCargo kind, read after the app own types and before file and layerRow. (5) The task candidate rule (Text for text, Fill for a shape) is incomplete: it says nothing about a screenshot wearing a Border, whose only colour lives in the Effects list rather than in layerPartRows, and nothing about a plain group or a bare picture, which have no colour at all and must refuse in words.

Opened the decision the task asked for rather than guessing: decision a-saved-colour-dropped-on-a-layer-row-paints-the-when-you-let-a-saved-colour-go-o, with the plain-language brief beside it. Four options, all written as what the line under the layers list would say: the layer main colour (recommended), every colour the layer paints, the row unfolds into its parts so you pick one, and leave colour off the list (marked as declining the task). Nothing was built, because every part of the build turns on the answer: the rule decides the sentence, the refusals and which layers can take a drop at all.

Shape of the build, for whoever picks this up after the answer. The row already reads what is in the air through DragCargo (Sources/Photonz/DragCargo.swift); adding colour is adding .color to LayerRowDropDelegate.takes in Sources/Photonz/LayersListView.swift and giving it a branch in dropEntered, dropUpdated, dropExited and performDrop beside the .textStyle one. The mark and the line are StyleRowDrop plus StyleRowMarking (Sources/PhotonzCore/StyleRowMarking.swift) and StyleRowDropNote (Sources/Photonz/InspectorSections.swift), all written around TextStyleDrop.Answer, so they need to carry a ColorDrop.Answer too. For the recommended option the rule is the first row of document.layerPartRows(layerIDs:) (Sources/PhotonzCore/LayerParts.swift), whose title is already the part name the sentence needs, falling through to the Border in the Effects list when the parts list is empty and the layer wears a ring (Layer.hasBorderColor in ColorStyles.swift), and refusing when neither is there. ColorDrop.Target takes that title as its part, so ColorDrop.answer writes the sentence unchanged. The drop itself is turnOnPart for a part with a switch and setPaint for one without, through History.perform so it is one undo step.

Waiting on the decision: when you let a saved colour go on a row in the layers list, what should it paint? Four options on the dashboard, brief beside the card. Nothing built, because the rule decides the sentence, the refusals and which rows can take a drop at all.
decision "When you let a saved colour go on a row in the layers list, what should it paint?" resolved: Its main colour, named before you let go

Decision resolved on 2026-09-13: "Its main colour, named before you let go". Second adversarial pass, now on the answer rather than the question. (1) The whole affordance is the line under the list: nothing about a layer row says it takes a colour, so the sentence naming the part BEFORE the drop is the feature, not decoration. The text style half proved the line works. (2) The rule resolves to one lookup that already exists: the first row of layerPartRows is the part the inspector leads with, so the list and the panel can never disagree about what a layer's main colour is. Fill for a box or a frame, Line for an arrow or a line, Text for words, Caliper for a measurement. (3) The two gaps the task named: a picture or a plain group wearing a Border has no parts row at all, so the Border in the Effects list is the fallback; one with no ring has no colour anywhere and must refuse in words. (4) Nothing to build for the sentence itself: ColorDrop.answer already writes "Paints Fill with Brand.", "Turns Fill on, painted with Brand." and the already-that-colour refusal, so the row reuses the swatch's own answer rather than growing a second voice. (5) One real model gap found: ColorDrop.Target.wearing is a non-optional Paint, and two of the three places that build one already fake it (Paint(hex:"#000000") with a comment apologising for it). A crowd of rows that disagree about what they wear has nothing honest to put there, and the fake white a Mixed swatch passes today makes a white colour dropped on Mixed refuse as a no-op. Making wearing optional is the smallest honest fix and it is what the crowd case needs.

Built and verified. CORE: Sources/PhotonzCore/ColorRowDrop.swift is the whole rule — PhotonzDocument.colorRowDrop works out the layer's main colour (first row of layerPartRows, falling through to the Border in the Effects list, refusing when there is neither), builds the same ColorDrop.Target a swatch builds and reads the same ColorDrop.answer back, so the list's sentence is the swatch's sentence; PhotonzDocument.paint(_:) lands it in ONE mutation (turnOnPart for an absent part, setPaint otherwise, then bindColorStyle for a name). 29 tests in Tests/PhotonzCoreTests/ColorRowDropTests.swift, written first. APP: EditorState+ColorRowDrop.swift, plus .color joining LayerRowDropDelegate.takes with its own branch in dropEntered/dropUpdated/performDrop (LayersListView.swift), gated on the existing next-color-drag flag so Current is untouched. StyleRowDrop now carries lands+note rather than a TextStyleDrop.Answer, with an init per kind, so one mark serves both tiles; sayTextStyleRowDrop/endTextStyleRowDrop renamed to sayStyleRowDrop/endStyleRowDrop for the same reason. WALK: Scripts/playtest/colour-onto-a-layer-row-walk.json, 82 steps, all seven cases green — Paints Fill with Brand, Fill is already Brand, Paints Text with Brand, Text is locked so it cannot be painted, Background has no colour to paint, Paints Border with Brand once it wears a ring, Paints Fill on both of them with Brand for a picked crowd. Scripts/test.sh 6557 tests green; colour (14), text-style (6), drop (7) and row- (33) walk fragments all green apart from measure-row-menu-walk, which the last sweep already had failing and which is folded into walks-that-fail-in-the-full-sweep with its reproduction.

Second adversarial pass, on the built thing, from the real screen captures the walk took (Screen Recording is granted, so these are the window as a person sees it). What works: the ring and the sentence arrive on the frame the pointer reaches the row, the accent plate for a yes and the dark plate with red dashes for a no are readable at a glance, and the refusals name the layer rather than the rule. One thing I changed away from the plan: nothing is armed for the next shape. A swatch drop arms the tool, but the row you aim at is not necessarily the row you have picked, so a tool quietly taking the colour of a layer somebody never selected is a surprise; the colour still joins the recents. LEFT ROUGH, below the follow-up bar and recorded here rather than filed: (1) the one line sits at the foot of the layers list and covers a word of the Canvas row underneath while a tile is in the air — transient, inherited from the text style drop which put the line there, and nothing is lost; (2) a saved colour turns out to be offered for every kind of colour row, so Brand saved off a fill lands on text wearing its name rather than only its colour — that is the existing behaviour of colorStyles(for:) on a swatch and changing it is a separate product question; (3) an arrow's head keeps its old colour when the shaft is repainted, which the decision named as the known cost of this rule and which the sentence warns about by saying Line.
